text:
maria: quick heads-up — I hacked up a prototype for live model swap that does slot reclamation without global stop-the-world. trying to reduce fragmentation when we evict large KV caches during a rollout.

alex: nice. is this the thing that uses a per-slot epoch + tombstone approach? last time that got tricky with refcounts.

maria: yup, per-slot epoch. idea: mark slot as `soft-dead` and allow inflight refs to drain; worker threads try to migrate live mappings off soft-dead slots to a transient buffer. once epoch confirms zero refs, we reclaim.

chris: sounds promethean. two quick concerns: (1) how do you prevent cascade reclaims under bursty load, (2) what's the impact on latency for small-batch 1–4 token requests?

maria: good Qs. for (1) I throttle reclamation with a credit-bucket per-tenant so only N slots can enter `soft-dead` concurrently. credits are earned by successful compaction/migration ops. for (2) migration is best-effort and uses a background coalesce thread; we keep hot-path token generation synchronous and hit an in-memory forwarding table for migrated pages. expected added p99 ~0.5–1ms in worst case.

sam: can you paste the proto/API you used for the slot control? would help to reason about portability to dedicated infra.

maria: here — rough sketch:

```
// Slot lifecycle API (sketch)
enum SlotState { ALIVE, SOFT_DEAD, MIGRATING, RECLAIMED }
struct SlotHeader { u64 slot_id; u64 epoch; SlotState state; u32 tenant_id; }
// callers: allocator->mark_soft_dead(slot_id) -> returns epoch
// worker: try_migrate(slot_id, epoch) -> success/try-later
// reclaim daemon: confirm_epoch_zero(epoch) -> free slot
```

alex: nice. question: who owns the forwarding table? global shard or per-queue? shared table might be hot.

maria: per-NUMA shard so lookups are local. we keep a small LRU of recent forwards; walkers consult the shard first then fall back to page-copy read path.

chris: corner case: what if migration repeatedly fails because target fragmentation is also high? could loop forever and starve reclaim credits.

maria: we have a backoff + demotion: after K failed attempts we mark the slot as `MIGRATING` with backpressure and expose a hint to scheduler to favor coalescing jobs for that tenant. if stage persists beyond T seconds, we escalate to `hard-free` which does a copy-on-free that clones the mapping and forces a synchronous memcopy (expensive but rare).

sam: that `hard-free` worries me for GPU pinned memory — memcopy to host has heavy cost. need safe fallback ordering and a limit so we don't thrash PCIe.

maria: agreed. plan is to only allow hard-free when tenant is below a low-priority threshold or during maintenance window. also PCIe rate-limit and per-node in-flight memcopy cap.

alex: telemetry ask: want counters for soft-dead entries, migration attempts/success, hard-free triggers, per-tenant reclaim-latency histogram. we should be able to alert before hard-free rate climbs.

infra-bot: noted — created ticket INFRA-3187 to add metrics hooks (maria -> owner). :white_check_mark:

chris: one more design thought: could we fold this into an allocator split API where allocators expose `prepare_release(slot_id)` and `finalize_release(slot_id)` so higher-level components (e.g., KV cache) can gracefully drain? keeps runtime generic.

maria: I like that. `prepare_release` would attempt to publish forward mappings and return a disposition (DEFERRED / READY / FORCE). `finalize_release` does the reclaim. I'll draft an RFC addendum for the allocator boundary.

sam: if you want, I can prototype the per-NUMA forwarding table and run small-batch latency microbenchmarks on the dev cluster this week.

maria: please do. action items: (1) maria — RFC addendum with `prepare_release`/`finalize_release` + API sketch, (2) alex — telemetry list + alert thresholds, (3) sam — perf prototype and microbench, (4) chris — review migration escalation policy. target sync in next infra sync.

alex: ack.

sam: ack, will start today.

maria: thanks all. I'll drop the RFC link here when it's ready.
